descriptions.pick_clean_then_place: Use when the task says clean, cleaned, wash, washed, or rinse an object (e.g. 'put a clean plate in the cabinet', 'rinse the mug and put it away'): take it, clean at the sinkbasin, then place it. Applies even if the destination is a microwave or fridge.
descriptions.pick_heat_then_place: Use when the task says heat, warm, hot, or cook an object (e.g. 'put a hot potato on the countertop', 'cook a plate of food then put it in the fridge'): heat in the microwave, then place it. Not for 'clean X in the microwave'. A microwave named only as the source is not a heat task.
descriptions.pick_two_obj_and_place: Use whenever the task has a count of two or a plural pair (e.g. 'put two smartphones on the sofa', 'two sets of keys in the safe', 'both newspapers on the stand'). 'Two' can be mid-sentence and any destination; find and place both, one at a time.
descriptions.pick_and_place: ALWAYS load for a plain single-object move with no heat/cool/clean word, no two-count, and no lamp-examine goal: take one object and put/move/take/throw it to a destination (e.g. 'put the phone on the dresser', 'move keys from desk to safe'). Also use when a lamp is only incidental and the goal is just placing. Don't load nothing.
descriptions.look_at_obj_in_light: Use only when the goal is to look at, examine, or inspect an object under a desklamp or floorlamp (e.g. 'look at the alarmclock under the desklamp', 'examine the statue with the lamp'). Involves turning on the lamp while holding the object. Not for ordinary placing tasks that merely mention a lamp.
